column1: # Every sim/mutate_*.sh, and whether a mutation anchor that matched ZERO
# times can be told apart from a mutation the checks tolerated.  The
# question is NOT whether a script spells the bug the same way; it is
# whether the OUTPUT of a no-op substitution differs from the output of a
# survivor.  A script can be safe by several routes and the route is named.
# class     SELFTEETH  carries a Z0 row whose BADMUT verdict is checked
#           GUARD      an anchor-failure path that cannot reach a verdict
#           RETIRED    a tombstone: it refuses to run and says what replaced it
# evidence  MEASURED   the script was RUN with an impossible anchor and the
#           DERIVED    classified from the guard mechanism, quoted, which
#                      returns before the design is built.  NOT run.
# sim/check_mutation_harness.py reads this file.  A new harness that is not
# listed here fails the audit: that is the way this defect comes back, since
# harnesses are written by copying an existing one.
